title: Out-of-order window sized for clock frequency
decision: Keep the out-of-order issue window and dispatch queues limited in size rather than making them large to maximize instruction-level parallelism.
rationale: The paper ties window size to cycle-time and wire-delay constraints: larger structures would lengthen critical paths and make the clock target harder.
outcome: The 21264 used a modest out-of-order window while preserving the high clock frequency that was central to its performance.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly discusses a rejected larger-window alternative or only states the chosen queue sizes.

title: Clustered integer execution
decision: Implement integer execution in two separate clusters, each with local execution resources and register-file state, rather than a single unified integer cluster.
rationale: Clustering reduced wire lengths and register-file porting complexity, helping the machine meet its high clock frequency.
outcome: The 21264's integer engine was organized as two cooperating clusters, with instruction steering/locality management across them.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly says a unified cluster was rejected or simply describes the clustered choice.

title: Instruction-cache replication for fetch timing
where_in_paper: Front end / physical-design or cache discussion
decision: Use replication of instruction-cache structures rather than relying on a single centralized multiported instruction cache.
rationale: Replication shortened long global wires and avoided the timing/complexity cost of a heavily ported central cache at the target clock.
outcome: The fetch/front-end path could be distributed locally, contributing to the wire-delay-driven floorplan and clock target.
weakest_point: Whether the paper says the instruction cache itself was replicated or only smaller fetch/queue structures were duplicated.

title: Wire-delay-driven floorplanning
decision: Drive the chip floorplan by wire-delay budgets, placing and duplicating major structures to control global interconnect delays.
rationale: At the 21264's target clock frequency, interconnect delay was a dominant constraint, so logic partitioning and placement had to be timing-driven.
outcome: The final microarchitecture/floorplan used local clusters and replicated structures to keep critical communication short.
weakest_point: Whether the paper uses the exact phrase wire-delay-driven or describes the same practice without naming it.
